name: Saint-Chinian

limits: For red and rosé wine, main grapes together: at least 60%
For red and rosé wine, Carignan and Cinsault together: at most 50%
For white wine, main grapes together: at least 70%
For white wine, Grenache Blanc: at least 20%
For white wine, Viognier: at most 10%
For red, rosé and white wine, grapes on trial together: at most 5%
rules.yield_base: 45 hl/ha for red, 54 for rosé, 50 for white

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.

notes: Syrah here goes into Rhône-style blends with Grenache, blends with Cabernet Sauvignon, and single-variety wines.
The vins doux naturels are sweet wines fortified with brandy to stop fermentation and keep their sugar.

blurb.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation for red, rosé and white wines, which must be blends of at least two grapes. Reds can use Syrah, Grenache, Carignan, Mourvèdre and Cinsault, and whites must include Grenache Blanc, with Marsanne, Roussanne and Vermentino as the other main grapes. It has had AOC protection since 1982.
